name: 20 Fenchurch Street
description: The tower gets wider as it goes up, so it looks top heavy on purpose. At the top there is a huge glass roof that sticks out over the street.

name: 111 West 57th Street
description: Thin terracotta piers run straight up the tower, which makes it look even narrower than it already is. It is the slimmest skyscraper in the world, and it sits on a very tight lot.

name: 1000 Trees
description: The building has rows of concrete columns, and each one holds a real tree on top. The columns step up like a terraced hill that someone dropped into the city.

name: Abbey of Mont Saint-Michel
description: Layers of granite climb the rock in a rough pyramid shape, which makes the abbey look like it grew straight out of the island.

name: Alhambra Palace
description: The palace is covered in detailed geometric tiles and has open courtyards, which give it a layered feel where one quiet space leads into the next.

name: Allianz Arena
description: Puffy diamond shaped panels cover the whole stadium in a soft skin, which lights up and changes color at night.

name: Amba Vilas Palace
description: Domes and arched walkways stack up in classic Indo-Saracenic style, which builds up toward a tall tower in the center.

name: Anfield
description: The stands are steep and lean in close to the pitch, which packs the crowd in tight and makes it loud.

name: Arch of Triumph
description: Heavy stone piers and a deep carved ceiling give the arch its strict symmetry. It stands right where a dozen big avenues meet.

name: ArtScience Museum
description: Ten petal shaped fingers open out from the base like a lotus flower, which catch rainwater and send it down to a pool in the middle.

name: Auditorium of Tenerife
description: A huge curved concrete roof sweeps up and over the building like a frozen wave, which hangs above the coastline.

name: Beijing National Stadium
description: Tangled steel beams wrap around the bowl of seats in a messy lattice, which is exactly why people call it the Bird's Nest.

name: Berlin Olympic Stadium
description: Heavy stone columns line up around a stadium that is sunk into the ground, which settles the whole thing low into the land.

name: Santiago Bernabeu Stadium
description: A shiny metal skin can open and close around the stands, which pulls a busy city stadium together into one smooth, reflective shape.

name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
description: A giant tilted disk of granite and glass leans toward the sea. Inside, it drops down into a wide reading room with stepped levels.

name: The Blue Mosque
description: Half domes step down from the main dome, and six thin minarets rise around it. They lead into a huge interior that is covered in tiles.

name: Buckingham Palace
description: A long, even classical front with a central entrance wraps around a big closed courtyard, which keeps the whole thing calm and symmetrical.

name: Fosun Foundation
description: Three layers of bronze tubes slowly turn around the building like a stage curtain, which opens and closes the view to the river.

name: Bulguksa Temple
description: Stone platforms and locked wooden brackets stack up in careful order, which lifts the wooden halls above the terraced hillside. It shows off Silla era craft.

name: Burj Al Arab
description: A big white sail made of coated fabric rises off its own man made island. Its shape comes from the sail of a traditional boat.

name: Burj Khalifa
description: The floor plan is a Y shape with three arms, which keeps the world's tallest tower stiff as it spirals up and cuts through the wind.

name: Camp Nou
description: Huge tilted concrete tiers stack outward to hold one of the biggest crowds in football, which all face inward toward the field.

name: Capital Gate
description: A diagonal steel frame lets the tower lean a bold 18 degrees to one side and still stay up, which braces it against wind and earthquakes.

name: Casa Batllo
description: Bony, uneven balconies and rippled colored tiles cover the front, which makes the building look almost alive, like it is made of bone and skin.

name: Casa Vicens
description: Patterned ceramic tiles and colorful brick cover the house in Moorish style decoration. It mixes straight lines with plant like detail, and it is one of Gaudi's earliest works.

name: Centre Pompidou
description: All the pipes, ducts, and structure are pushed to the outside and color coded, which leaves the floors inside wide open and easy to change around.

name: Chapel on the Water
description: Two L shaped concrete walls frame the view outside, which sets the plain, quiet chapel right at the edge of a still pond.

name: Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore
description: A massive double shell brick dome, which was a risky piece of engineering back then, sits above a front that is covered in patterned marble.

name: Church of Light
description: A cross is cut clean through a bare concrete wall, which lets a cross of bright daylight do all the decoration inside.

name: Coal Drops Yard
description: Two old Victorian coal sheds got new curved roofs that reach toward each other, which forms a covered street between the brick buildings.

name: Cologne Cathedral
description: Stone tracery and thin buttresses push straight up in a dense, sharp lattice, which looks like it pierces the sky.

name: Colosseum
description: Stacked rows of arches and stepped stone tiers ring the arena, which is built from layer on layer of vaults.

name: DDP(Dongdaemun Design Plaza)
description: Smooth aluminum panels and soft curves let the building bend and roll like a landscape, which has no hard edges anywhere.

name: Dubai Frame
description: A giant gold rectangle stands empty in the middle, which frames old Dubai on one side and new Dubai on the other.

name: Eiffel Tower
description: Open iron lattice lets you see right through the tower as it gets narrower toward the top. The metal web is built so the wind passes through it.

name: Empire State Building
description: Stepped Art Deco setbacks climb to a sharp vertical peak, which helped define the New York skyline.

name: Emporia
description: A curved wall of golden glass gives the building a soft, liquid look on the outside, even though it is solid underneath.

name: Fallingwater
description: Concrete decks reach out over a stream, which anchors the house into the rock so it looks like it grew there.

name: Ferrari World Abu Dhabi
description: A wide red roof spreads low and flat over the building, and its curves come straight from the body of a sports car.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza(Pyramid of Khufu)
description: Layer after layer of stone narrows to a single point with almost perfect accuracy. It is simple geometry built at a huge scale.

name: Guggenheim Abu Dhabi
description: Cones and blocks pile together into a rough, sculptural mass, which echoes the desert and refuses to settle into one neat shape.

name: Guggenheim Bilbao Museum
description: Curved sheets of titanium ripple across the building, which blurs the line between architecture and sculpture.

name: Guggenheim Museums
description: One long spiral ramp turns the museum into a walk, so you go down past the art instead of room to room.

name: Gwangan Bridge
description: Steel cables stretch across the water in an even rhythm, and the long deck reads as one clean line on the horizon.

name: Hagia Sophia
description: A massive dome sits over the main hall and looks like it floats. It rests on curved supports, which spread the weight out and keep the inside open and full of light.

name: Heydar Aliyev Center
description: The walls and floors blend into one smooth curve, so the outside and the inside flow together with no clear line between them.

name: Island-bridge Murinzel
description: Steel walkways cross over each other to form a small man made island in the river, which becomes a public spot you can reach from several sides.

name: Jongmyo Shrine
description: Long, low rows of plain wooden halls repeat in a steady horizontal beat. That quiet sameness is what gives the shrine its solemn, calm feeling.

name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
description: Layered roof brackets and wide, curved rooflines stack in careful order, which shows off traditional Korean wood joinery.

name: Liege-Guillemins Railway Station
description: Thin steel ribs arch up into a wide glass roof, which makes the station feel like it opens straight into the city.

name: London Stadium
description: A light roof rings the field in a clean circle, and cables hold it up so the pitch sits inside a thin, clear frame.

name: Lotte Giants Sajik Stadium
description: Tiered concrete stands curve around the field, which pulls the crowd into one tight, loud bowl.

name: Lotte World Tower
description: Glass walls get slightly narrower as they rise, which brings the tower to a slim, crystal like point at the top.

name: Lotus Temple
description: Nine clusters of white concrete petals open like a lotus flower, which gather around one quiet space for prayer.

name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
description: A huge dome full of small holes filters the sunlight into a pattern of dots that moves through the day, which people call a 'rain of light.' It floats over the white galleries below.

name: Market Hall (Rotterdam)
description: A giant horseshoe arch of apartments curves overhead, and a busy covered market fills the open space underneath.

name: Marina Bay Sands
description: Three towers hold up one long deck across the top, which ties the three legs together into a single line on the skyline.

name: Mercedes-Benz Stadium
description: The roof opens and closes like a camera shutter. Eight panels slide back, which leaves a round eye open above the field.

name: Merdeka 118
description: Triangular glass facets cover the tower like a cut gem, which climb up to a slim spire that sits off to one side.

name: Metropol Parasol
description: A huge wooden lattice spreads out overhead like a group of giant mushrooms, which shades the plaza below.

name: Milan Cathedral
description: A forest of marble spires and flying buttresses points upward, which breaks the heavy stone into a spiky, lacy skyline.

name: Milwaukee Art Museum
description: Two steel wings open and close over the entrance like a bird, which controls how much daylight comes in.

name: Morpheus
description: An outer frame wraps the hotel and leaves big holes right through the middle, which holds the whole building up from the outside.

name: Museum of the Future
description: A smooth ring shaped building is wrapped in Arabic calligraphy, and the words are cut right through the wall so light comes inside.

name: Namsan Seoul Tower
description: A thin lattice mast on top of the mountain adds even more height, which lifts the lookout deck high over the whole city.

name: National Centre for the Performing Arts
description: A smooth titanium and glass dome sits in a pool of water like a half sunk egg, which breaks up the strict grid of the city around it.

name: National Palace Museum
description: Yellow glazed tiles and curved up eaves carry traditional palace style up the hillside in a grand, formal way.

name: National Palace of Pena
description: A jumble of colorful towers in styles that clash crowds the mountaintop. It is fully romantic and mismatched on purpose.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
description: Uneven limestone towers and battlements pile up into a heavily decorated castle that looks like it came from a fairy tale. It sits on a rocky alpine peak.

name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
description: Flying buttresses lean in from the outside to hold up the tall stone walls. They take the sideways push, which lets the nave rise so high.

name: Oculus Transportation Hub World Trade Center
description: Ribbed white steel spreads out like the wings of a bird, and daylight pours down through the gaps into the transit hall below.

name: Old Trafford
description: Steel roofs reach out over the pitch, which pulls the crowd noise in tight around the field.

name: One World Trade Center, 1WTC
description: Eight slanted triangle faces twist the square base into a tall, crystal like spire, which cuts through the wind as it rises.

name: Oracle Park
description: Red brick gives the ballpark an old, factory like feel, and the open side frames the bay as part of the view from the seats.

name: Orsay Museum
description: Exposed iron trusses, which are left over from its days as a train station, arch over a long hall full of light.

name: Osaka Castle
description: Stepped stone walls rise like a fortress, which lifts the gold trimmed keep up above its moat and park.

name: Oscar Niemeyer Museum
description: A giant concrete eye sits up on a stem above a flat, mirror like base, which makes it look like it floats off the ground.

name: Palace of Versailles
description: Long sight lines and a repeated, even front give the palace its strict symmetry, which carries straight out into the gardens.

name: Palais Garnier
description: Gold trimmed stone and layered marble pile on the Beaux-Arts richness, which steers you toward the grand hall inside.

name: Pantheon
description: A coffered half dome finishes off a perfect round interior. A single round hole at the top lets daylight pour straight down.

name: Park Guell
description: Wavy walls covered in broken tile mosaic snake across the slope, which follow the land so the building and the hill blend together.

name: Petra
description: Classical fronts are carved straight into the sandstone cliff, which ties the building to the layered rock of the canyon.

name: Petronas Twin Tower
description: Star shaped floor plates, which come from Islamic patterns, stack into twin towers that are joined partway up by a skybridge.

name: Phillips Exeter Academy Library
description: Plain brick walls stack into a simple cube. Inside, the rooms are arranged around a tall central hall that is full of light.

name: Potala Palace
description: Stepped stone walls climb the hillside like a fortress, which follow the rough shape of the slope.

name: Prague Castle
description: Centuries of walls, towers, and gothic spires pile into one big hilltop complex, which looms over the city.

name: Royal Palace of Madrid
description: Plain, massive limestone and granite walls keep things strict and horizontal, which squares the building off around a huge courtyard.

name: Sagrada Familia
description: Tree like stone columns split apart as they rise, which fills the church like a forest. Tall spires shoot up over the whole thing.

name: Sainte-Chapelle
description: Walls of stained glass take the place of most of the stone, which turns the chapel into a glass cage full of bright, colored light.

name: Salk Institute for Biological Studies
description: Bare concrete blocks form two identical wings, which frame an open stone courtyard that looks straight out to the ocean.

name: San Siro Stadium
description: Spiral concrete ramps wind up the outside of the stadium, which hold up the roof over the steep rows of seats.

name: Santa Maria de Montserrat Abbey
description: Rough stone walls rise to match the jagged cliffs around them, so the monastery looks like it was carved out of the mountain.

name: Schonbrunn Palace
description: An even yellow front stretches out long and low, which links the formal courtyard to the gardens behind it.

name: Seokguram Grotto
description: Granite blocks are fitted together with exact math into a small domed cave, which points the viewer toward the carved Buddha in the center.

name: Seoul Olympic Stadium
description: Curved concrete tiers flare out in a wide oval, and the shape is based on a traditional Korean pot. The field sits sunk in the middle.

name: Shanghai Tower
description: A glass skin twists as it climbs, which actually helps the tower shed the wind on the way up.

name: Southern Branch of the National Palace Museum
description: Curved shapes that overlap each other borrow the feel of ink wash painting, which settles the museum into the lake around it.

name: Sphere
description: The whole outside is one seamless LED screen wrapped over a perfect sphere, and the inside has projection that wraps all the way around you.

name: St. Basil's Cathedral
description: Brightly colored onion domes cluster together at different heights, which packs the church with dense, playful detail.

name: St. Peter's Basilica
description: Giant Corinthian columns and a huge central dome set the scale, which frames the big square out front.

name: Statue of Liberty
description: A copper skin over an iron frame stands tall and upright, which faces out toward the harbor.

name: Sunrise Kempinski Hotel
description: A round glass front turns the whole hotel into a giant ball that looks like a sun that sits low on the shoreline.

name: Sydney Opera House
description: Locked together concrete shells rise like a group of sails, which lift up sharply off the edge of the harbour.

name: Taichung Green Museumbrary
description: Stacked shapes full of holes and gaps mix the library and the park together, which blurs where the building ends and the green space starts.

name: Taipei 101
description: Stacked sections get a bit narrower as they go up, like a pagoda, and a giant pendulum inside keeps the tower steady in the wind.

name: Taipei Dome
description: One big curved shell holds all the tension of the steel roof in a single smooth shape.

name: Taj Mahal
description: Perfectly balanced marble faces sit in flawless symmetry, which makes the heavy building look like it floats in its own pool of light.

name: TAO ZHU YIN YUAN
description: The floors twist as they go up in a double helix, and plants cover the whole thing, which makes the tower look like a green spiral that climbs upward.

name: The Forbidden City
description: Everything lines up on one strict central axis, walled courtyard after walled courtyard, which lays out the old imperial order in stone and wood.

name: The Louvre Museum
description: Glass pyramid facets sit against the old stone courtyards. The sharp modern shape leads visitors down into the museum below.

name: The Parthenon
description: Evenly spaced columns set up a steady beat, and tiny built in curves trick your eye, which makes the temple look perfectly straight.

name: The Shard
description: Faceted glass panels catch and scatter the sky, which makes the tower look like it fades away toward its sharp top.

name: The Vessel
description: Bronze staircases cross over each other into an open maze of landings, which is built just for walking up and around.

name: Tokyo Dome
description: A tight fabric roof is held up by the air pressure inside, which gives the stadium one big open space with nothing in the way.

name: Tokyo Skytree
description: A lattice tower that gets thinner as it rises borrows from old triangular wood frames, which lets it reach record height and stay steady.

name: Topkapi Palace
description: A chain of walled courtyards, where each one is more private than the last, lays the palace out as a series of gated thresholds.

name: Tottenham Hotspur Stadium
description: Steep, close stands wrap the pitch in one tight bowl, which traps the crowd noise and aims it at the field.

name: Trocadero Square
description: A wide open axis lines up the city's sight lines, which frames a grand view straight across to the Eiffel Tower.

name: Wembley Stadium
description: One huge steel arch carries the weight of the roof in a single span, which anchors the round bowl in the city around it.

name: Westminster Abbey
description: Ribbed stone vaults carry the weight up and overhead, which makes the heavy stone feel light and pulls your eye toward the windows.

name: Yankee Stadium
description: A formal stone front wraps the ballpark in a solid, classic shell, which tightens the big field into a close, high energy arena.

name: Villa Savoye
description: A plain white box that floats on thin columns, which stands for Le Corbusier's idea of a modern 'machine for living.'

name: Frank Lloyd Wright Home
description: The house grew over the years as Wright's own home and workshop, where he tested his ideas.

name: Casa Mila
description: A wavy line that stands for the rippled stone front, which earned the building its nickname 'the quarry.'

name: Azadi Tower
description: White marble covers a tower built as one giant arch. The curve mixes an old Persian arch with a pointed Islamic one, and the legs split apart and meet again at the top.

name: Bauhaus
description: A glass wall wraps the corner of the workshop block, which lets you see the structure right through it. The whole building is plain, white, and boxy, and the famous BAUHAUS sign runs straight down the side.

name: Kowloon Walled City
description: A tight, messy block of stacked shapes, which stands for the most crowded place on earth that once stood here.

name: The Great Wall of China
description: A wavy line with watchtowers, which stands for the wall as it winds over the mountains.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
description: A round tower that tilts to one side, which is the famous lean everyone knows it for.

name: Church of St. Ignatius of Loyola at Campus Martius
description: The ceiling looks like it opens into a huge dome, but it is really flat and painted with a trick of perspective.

name: Trevi Fountain
description: The figure of a sea god in front of arches, which stands for the grand Baroque fountain.

name: Piazza Navona
description: A long oval with a fountain in the middle, which traces the old Roman racetrack the square was built on.

name: Castle of the Holy Angel
description: An angel on top of a round tower, which is the archangel the castle is named for.

name: St. Paul's Cathedral
description: A round dome with a cross on top, which stands for Christopher Wren's famous cathedral.

name: Elizabeth Tower
description: A tall clock tower shape, which everyone knows as the face of London.

name: King's Cross Station
description: A fan of curved lines that spread out from one point, which copies the station's curved roof.

name: Tower Bridge
description: Two towers joined by a high walkway over a road that splits open, which is the bridge's famous shape.

name: Cube House
description: A cube balanced on one corner, which is the odd tilted shape of the houses.

name: Art Depot Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen
description: A round mirror bowl that reflects the city, which stands for the first open art storage building in the world.

name: St. Stephen's Cathedral
description: A steep roof with a colorful zigzag pattern, which is the tiled roof everyone knows this church by.

name: Hohensalzburg Fortress
description: A fortress on a hilltop, which stands for one of the biggest old castles still left in Europe.

name: Machu Picchu
description: Stone terraces below a sharp peak, which is the view everyone pictures of the lost Inca city.

name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
description: A letter M drawn from an old Renaissance diagram of circles and lines, which links the museum to classical art.

name: Pyramid of the Moon
description: A stepped pyramid shape, which stands for one of the great pyramids of ancient Mexico.

name: Christ the Redeemer
description: A figure with arms spread wide, which is the statue that watches over Rio.

name: Angkor Wat
description: Five towers shaped like lotus buds, which is the temple outline seen on Cambodia's flag.

name: The British Museum
description: A row of Greek columns, which stands for the museum's grand front and its ancient collections.

name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
description: Curved metal sails that seem to move, which stands for the hall's curved steel shape.

name: Willis Tower
description: Nine squares bundled together at different heights, which shows how the tower is built.

name: Goldengate bridge
description: Two tall towers linked by long curved cables, which is the outline of the famous orange bridge.

name: CN Tower
description: A thin tower with a round pod near the top, which is the shape that marks Toronto's skyline.

name: Palm Jumeirah
description: A palm tree seen from above, which is the shape of the man-made islands.

name: Apple Park
description: A perfect ring, which stands for the round main building at Apple's headquarters.

name: Suzhou Museum of Contemporary Art
description: A ribbon that curves over grouped shapes, which stands for the long roof that ties the pavilions together.

name: Zaishui Art Museum
description: A long, thin line low over water, which stands for the museum that sits right on a lake.

name: Margravial Opera House
description: A Baroque theater where the whole inside is carved and painted wood, so the plain outside hides a rich, layered hall within.

name: National Theatre Munich
description: A row of tall Greek columns fronts a steep triangular roof, which gives the opera house the look of a classical temple.

name: Weissenhof Estate
description: Plain white boxes with flat roofs and open plans sit together as a test estate, which showed off early modern housing ideas.

name: National Museum of Korea
description: A long, low stone building splits into two wings with a wide open gap between them, which frames a view straight through to the mountain behind.

name: The Getty Center
description: Blocks of pale travertine stone step across a hilltop, which spread the museum out into pavilions linked by open courtyards.

name: Spaceship Earth
description: A full geodesic sphere is built from thousands of triangles, which is the only complete sphere of its kind you can walk inside.

name: Oslo Opera House
description: A sloped white marble roof runs straight down into the water like a ramp, which invites people to walk right up over the building.

name: Dubai Opera
description: The curved glass shape copies a traditional wooden sailing boat, which nods to the region's pearl fishing past.

name: The Royal Danish Library
description: A sleek black granite and glass block leans over the water, which earned it the nickname 'the Black Diamond.'

name: City of Arts and Sciences
description: White skeleton like shells and long pools spread across the site, which turn the science complex into a set of giant sculptures.

name: Villa Rotunda
description: A perfectly symmetrical house with the same temple front on all four sides sits under a central dome, which is a model of Renaissance balance.

name: Chichu Art Museum
description: Most of the museum is buried underground, so bare concrete rooms are lit only by daylight that drops in through open cuts above.

name: Leeum, Samsung Museum of Art
description: Three buildings by three different architects sit side by side, which mixes terracotta, black concrete, and glass into one museum.

name: Flatiron Building
description: A wedge shaped tower fills a sharp triangular corner, which squeezes to a narrow point where two avenues cross.

name: House VI
description: Grids, walls, and columns cut through the house in ways that ignore how you actually live, which treats the home as a pure geometric puzzle.

name: Cusco Cathedral
description: Heavy Spanish stone walls sit right on top of old Inca foundations, which stacks two very different building traditions in one place.

name: Couvent de La Tourette
description: A raw concrete monastery sits up on legs over a slope, which wraps plain monk cells around an inner courtyard.

name: Philip Johnson Glass House
description: The outer walls are all glass, so the house is fully see through and the surrounding landscape becomes the real wall.

name: Casa da Musica
description: A faceted white concrete block full of odd angles sits alone on an open plaza, which looks like a rough cut stone dropped in the city.

name: Spiral Building
description: A staggered mix of shapes and a spiral ramp stack up the front, which breaks the busy street wall into playful, mismatched pieces.

name: Vitra Fire Station
description: Sharp concrete planes slice and tilt at hard angles, which makes the little fire station look frozen mid movement.

name: Vitra Design Museum
description: White curved walls and ramps twist and collide, which turns the small museum into a piece of abstract sculpture.

name: HSBC Main Building
description: The structure is hung from big outer masts and braces, which clears the ground floor into an open public space you can walk right under.

name: Loyd's Building
description: Stairs, lifts, and pipes are all pushed to the outside, which leaves the trading floors inside as one big open, flexible space.

name: 425 park avenue
description: The tower steps back three times as it rises and shows off its bracing at the top, which gives it a clear, structured skyline profile.

name: The Shed
description: A giant outer shell on wheels rolls out over an open plaza, which doubles the size of the arts center when it is needed.

name: Couvent Sainte-Marie de La Tourette
description: A raw concrete monastery perches on thin legs over a slope, which lines up plain monk cells above a shared courtyard.

name: Villa d'Este
description: Terraced gardens step down the hillside past hundreds of fountains, which turn moving water into the main show of the villa.

name: Museum SAN
description: Stone, water, and paper themed courtyards line up in a row, which lead visitors slowly through calm space before reaching the art.

name: Le Corbusier's Cabanon
description: A tiny plain wood cabin holds everything needed to live in one small room, which was Le Corbusier's test of the smallest good home.

name: Hemeroscopium House
description: Heavy concrete and steel beams balance on top of each other like a stack of giant blocks, which lock together with a pool as the counterweight.

name: The Factory
description: Old brick industrial buildings are joined by new additions, which keep the raw factory feel while turning it into an arts space.

name: The Aalto House
description: Brick, wood, and white render mix softly across a home and studio, which blends work and living into one warm, natural whole.

name: Ronchamp Chapel
description: Thick curved white walls and a heavy sweeping roof bend in odd directions, which scatter small colored windows through the dim chapel.

name: Brother Klaus Field Chapel
description: A rough concrete tower was cast around a stack of logs that was then burned away, which leaves a charred, cave like room open to the sky.

name: 7132 Therme
description: Stacked local quarry stone forms the bath house, which channels visitors through narrow stone passages into pools of different temperatures.

name: Reichstag Building
description: A new glass dome sits on top of the old stone parliament, which lets people walk up a spiral ramp right above the debating chamber.

name: Kimbell Art Museum
description: A row of long concrete vaults runs side by side, and a thin slit at the top of each one washes soft daylight across the galleries.

name: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library
description: The walls are thin panels of marble that glow when the sun shines through, which protects the rare books from harsh light.

name: Citigroup Center
description: The tower stands on four huge columns set at the middle of each side, which lifts the whole building up and leaves the corners open.

name: CCTV Headquarters
description: Two leaning towers bend and join at the top and bottom into a giant loop, which forms a bold, twisted ring in the sky.

name: Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth
description: Glass pavilions sit in a reflecting pool with concrete roofs on Y shaped columns, which makes the building seem to float on water.

name: Renzo Pavilion
description: A light steel and glass roof floats above the galleries, which filters daylight down evenly so the art below is softly lit.

name: Amon Carter Museum of American Art
description: A calm portico of pale stone arches faces the city, which sets a quiet, classical front for the art inside.

name: 30 St Mary Axe
description: A rounded glass tower narrows at both ends and spirals with dark bands, which earned it the nickname 'the Gherkin.'

name: National Museum of Qatar
description: Hundreds of flat sand colored disks interlock in every direction, which copy the crystals of a desert rose stone.

name: Farnsworth House
description: A single glass room floats on white steel columns above a flood plain, which strips the house down to a clear, open box.

name: Barcelona Pavilion
description: Thin marble walls and a flat roof float over open space, which lets rooms flow into each other with almost no doors.

name: Tour Triangle
description: A flat triangular slab is wide at the base and thin at the top, which looks solid from the front and razor thin from the side.

name: National Parliament House
description: Bare concrete blocks with huge geometric cut outs ring a central chamber, which brings daylight deep into the assembly.

name: Santa Justa Lift
description: A tall iron tower with an open lattice frame lifts people between two street levels, which looks like a piece of the Eiffel Tower in the city.

name: Luis Barragan House and Studio
description: Plain walls painted in bold colors frame quiet rooms and small courtyards, which use light and color instead of decoration.

name: Al Bahar Towers
description: A shading skin of folding umbrella like panels wraps the twin towers, which open and close with the sun to cut the desert heat.

name: Ali Qapu Palace
description: A tall gate palace has a high covered balcony held up by slim wooden columns, which looks out over the grand royal square.

name: Bahrain World Trade Center
description: Two sail shaped towers hold three wind turbines on bridges between them, which turn the gap between the towers into a power source.

name: Bosco Verticale
description: Two apartment towers are covered in hundreds of real trees and shrubs on every balcony, which makes a vertical forest in the city.

name: Bullitt Center
description: A big solar roof overhangs the whole building, which lets the office make all its own power and water to run fully green.

name: Church of Saint-Maclou
description: A lacy, heavily carved stone front bristles with sharp Gothic detail, which packs delicate tracery across the whole facade.

name: DFAB House (NEST)
description: Parts of the house were built by robots and 3D printers, which shows off odd curved shapes normal building could not make.

name: Elbphilharmonie Hamburg
description: A wavy glass concert hall sits on top of an old brick warehouse, which stacks a modern crown on a heavy industrial base.

name: Finlandia Hall
description: A white marble concert hall with a slanted tower keeps clean, calm lines, which reflects Alvar Aalto's soft modern style.

name: Harpa Concert Hall and Conference Centre
description: A glass skin made of colored honeycomb cells covers the hall, which catches the northern light like fish scales.

name: Maison de Verre (House of Glass)
description: The front wall is built from glass blocks that glow with light, which fills the home with soft daylight while keeping it private.

name: Paimio Sanatorium
description: Long, thin wings with wide balconies face the sun, which was designed down to the furniture to help patients heal.

name: Rolex Learning Center (EPFL)
description: One flowing concrete floor gently rolls up and down with holes cut through it, which turns the whole building into a single open landscape.

name: Seagram Building
description: A clean bronze and glass tower is set back behind an open plaza, which became the model for the modern glass office block.

name: Sendai Mediatheque
description: See through floors are held up by hollow tube like columns, which lets you look straight through the glass building from outside.

name: National Theatre of Costa Rica
description: A grand stone front with columns and statues copies European opera houses, which brought old world splendor to Central America.

name: Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art
description: Curved concrete scoops on the roof catch daylight like wind towers, which mix modern shapes with old Persian building tricks.

name: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa
description: A low round glass building has no clear front or back, which lets visitors enter and wander from any side.

name: Vasconcelos Library
description: Glass and steel book stacks seem to float in a tall open hall, which turns the whole library into one big transparent volume.

name: Boston City Hall
description: Heavy concrete blocks jut out over a brick plaza in bold Brutalist style, which puts the building's structure right on show.

name: Botin Art Centre
description: Two rounded pods clad in shiny tiles float on slim columns over the waterfront, which lift the galleries up to open the ground below.

name: Gardens by the Bay
description: Giant tree shaped steel towers hold real plants and gather solar power, which mixes a garden and a machine into one skyline.

name: High Line
description: An old raised train line was turned into a long thin park, which threads a green walkway right through the city buildings.

name: Seattle Central Library
description: A faceted glass and steel skin folds around stacked, shifted boxes, which spirals the book collection up through the building.

name: Tate Modern
description: A huge old power station was reused as an art museum, which kept the giant turbine hall as one vast open gallery.

name: The Holy Redeemer Church and Community Centre of Las Chumberas
description: Plain white concrete blocks shift and split apart, which let thin lines of daylight slip into the simple worship space.

name: 41 Cooper Square
description: A perforated metal skin peels open at the entrance and a twisting stair runs up the middle, which links all the floors through one dramatic core.

name: Gando Primary School
description: A raised tin roof floats above the classrooms to pull hot air out, which keeps the local clay walls cool without any power.

name: Healing Stay KOSMOS (Kosmos Ulleungdo)
description: Curved white concrete walls wrap around an open courtyard on a remote island, which frames the sea and sky as part of the retreat.

name: Neue Staatsgalerie Stuttgart
description: Stone walls, bright color accents, and a round open courtyard mix old and new, which lets a public path wind right through the museum.

name: Ningbo History Museum
description: The walls are built from broken tiles and bricks salvaged from torn down villages, which packs local history right into the building's skin.

name: Municipal Stadium of Braga
description: The stadium is cut into a rock quarry with stands on only two sides, which are linked across the top by steel cables like a bridge.

name: Ibere Camargo Foundation
description: A white concrete block sprouts curving outer ramps that snake down its face, which carry visitors between the stacked galleries.

name: MAXXI - National Museum of 21st Century Arts
description: Long curved concrete tubes bend and overlap through the building, which pull visitors along flowing paths instead of square rooms.

name: The Menil Collection Museum
description: A long, low building uses curved white 'leaves' in the roof to bounce soft daylight into the galleries, which lights the art without harsh sun.
